games.title: Grim Gambit
games.tagline: Lead the company. Bury the dead. Do not look back.
games.description: A dark gothic, turn-based tactics game in the style of XCOM. Lead a company of ten classes against undead, demons and vampires across haunted graveyards, burning pits, flooded crypts and ruined cathedrals. Build fighters from thirty Diablo II-style talent trees, loot, set gear, runes and a forge. Every New Game+ raises the stakes, and the online Top 100 ranks every company by how far it has gone.

download.label: Download Beta 0.1.6
download.note: Windows: extract the zip anywhere and run Grim Gambit.exe. The launcher updates you to the latest version. If Windows shows a SmartScreen warning, click More info → Run anyway. Phones, tablets and Macs: press Play in browser. On a phone, use Add to Home Screen to play fullscreen like an app.

patchNotes.title: Matching cards
notes: The hover cards in battle now match the squad screen: name, class and level, a health bar, stats in a grid, status tags (Burning, Hidden, Overwatch, Hunkered, Panicked...), abilities with cooldowns and gear for your fighters, and a short description plus your chance to hit for enemies.
Ability button tooltips use the same dark-and-gold style.
Already playing on Windows? Open the launcher and it downloads this update automatically. The browser version is already updated.

patchNotes.title: Into the light
notes: New squad screen: your company waits in a dark, foggy castle hall, and the fighters you pick for the squad step into shafts of light. Click a fighter to bring them into the light or send them back into the dark; big companies stand in a zig-zag so nobody hides behind anyone.
Hover over a fighter (or press and hold on a phone) to see their level, health, stats, abilities and gear.
Marching out with fewer than 6 fighters now asks first, so you don't leave someone behind by accident.
The build number and cloud save status moved to the top-right corner, so they no longer overlap your gold in the bottom-right.
Already playing on Windows? Open the launcher and it downloads this update automatically. The browser version is already updated.

patchNotes.title: Smooth menus
notes: Fixed big stutters in the menus: the game no longer keeps drawing the last battlefield hidden behind full-screen menus like the title screen, barracks, gear and shops.
You can always select your own fighters in battle, even on the enemy's turn or with Auto on, to see their card and ability bar. The bar is greyed out until it's their turn to act.
Fullscreen is back on the main menu, and also in Options: one click to switch between fullscreen and windowed (F11 still works). Borderless windowed is under Options → Graphics.
Already playing on Windows? Open the launcher and it downloads this update automatically. The browser version is already updated.

patchNotes.title: Blood and phones
notes: Big performance boost in bloody battles: blood that has finished spreading is painted into a single floor layer instead of hundreds of separate splashes, so the frame rate holds up even on Excessive gore.
Fewer stutters when blood first appears, and blood splashing onto props is cheaper to work out.

Grim Gambit now plays in the browser on phones and tablets, at fletchergames.github.io/play: pinch to zoom, two fingers to pan, drag to turn the camera, and press and hold on an enemy or tile to see hit chances and cover.
Cloud saves work across the desktop game and the browser version: sign in with the same account to continue anywhere.
Already playing on Windows? Open the launcher and it downloads this update automatically.

patchNotes.title: Quiet in the ranks
notes: Removed the spoken voice lines and the speech bubbles over fighters. Panic, bonds and morale still work, and still show in the battle log.
Hit chances now show as whole numbers in the battle log and the hover tooltip.
Fixed the enemy hover card staying on screen into the next battle.
Already playing? Open the launcher and it downloads this update automatically.

patchNotes.title: Tactics of the Damned
notes: Bigger battlefields: every map is now 22 by 20 tiles, with room to flank, fall back and fight over objectives.

Half and full cover: graves, crates and low walls give −20% to be hit; pillars, statues and trees give −40%. Every prop shows its shield during deployment, and you can hold C or press Cover to see them any time.
High ground: raised stone platforms give +15% aim against targets below.
Hit-chance preview: hover an enemy to see every modifier behind your chance to hit, plus damage and whether the shot is lethal.
Blue and gold movement: blue tiles keep an action to attack, gold tiles are a dash that spends both. Hovering a tile shows its cover and warns of enemy overwatch.
Hunker Down: brace behind cover for double protection until your next turn.
Missed shots fly past the target and slam into the ground or the cover it hides behind.
Destructible battlefield: cover cracks and collapses under fire, and volatile barrels explode.
Morale and panic, with voice lines: losing a friend or taking a brutal hit can make a fighter flee, cower or fire wildly. Voice lines can be turned off in Options.
Bonds: fighters who survive battles together form bonds for better aim side by side, steadier nerves, and vengeance when their partner is hurt.
New objectives: stop the ritual, rescue the captive, break through to the gate, or hold the line, each with a turn limit and bonus gold.
The three campaign bosses are now drawn at random from all ten every campaign, and are scaled to their place on the road. A campaign in progress re-rolls the bosses you haven't fought yet.
New tutorials for your first battle and for returning from it, covering cover shields, high ground, objectives, barrels, Hunker Down, panic and bonds. Replay them any time from Options.
Already playing? Open the launcher and it downloads this update automatically.

patchNotes.title: Ready for battle
notes: New first-campaign tutorial: a step-by-step guide through the Barracks, skill trees, gear, the campaign map and choosing your squad. Each step lights up what to click, with an arrow and a short explanation.
A little bell rings whenever a tutorial step or tip pops up.

Targeting: clicking an enemy now targets it instead of attacking. Press Attack, now the first slot on the ability bar (hotkey 1), or an attack ability to strike your target. Your whole squad can focus the same target.
New Options → Graphics screen: windowed, fullscreen or borderless windowed, resolution, quality, frame rate limit, brightness and an FPS counter.
Cloud saves: the game now asks on launch if you’d like to connect an account, and your login stays saved on your PC. If a login ever expires, you’re asked to sign back in with your email filled in.
Fixed the old main menu flashing for a moment when the game opens.
Removed the Fullscreen button from the main menu. Use F11, Alt+Enter, or Options → Graphics.
Players on Beta 0.1: download this version once and extract it over your old folder. Your saves are kept.

patchNotes.title: The company marches
notes: Grim Gambit is now a desktop game with its own launcher. Patches download automatically when you open it.
Cloud saves: the game saves after every move and backs up online within seconds. Make an account to continue on any PC.
Resume Battle: quit mid-fight and pick up exactly where you left off.
Online Top 100 leaderboard, ranked by highest New Game+ reached.
Ten classes and thirty talent trees, with capstone masteries and 30 matching item sets.
Loot: affixes, legendary, mythic and cursed items, runes, sockets and a forge.
Living maps with lava, swamps, thunderstorms and a mad organist in the Black Chapel.
Reactive gore with damage-type deaths. Bodies become cover. Gore can be set to Off, Normal or Excessive.

games.summary: My playable dark fantasy tactics project. Lead a company through gothic battlefields, build your fighters, and see how far you can take them.

games.title: Gangland: Empire Burning
games.tagline: Build your crew. Take the streets. Rule an empire.
games.description: Gangland: Empire Burning is an in-development remaster project built around the original Gangland’s blend of crime strategy, crew command, business management and rival gangs. The goal is to preserve its gameplay and setting while rebuilding the experience for modern Windows PCs and iPhone and iPad: clearer controls, a redesigned interface, refreshed presentation and more of the world to explore.
games.screenshotNote: Recovered character, vehicle and environment assets from our inspection and conversion work. These development renders show the starting point for the remaster, with original textures and approximate lighting; they are not final gameplay screenshots.

screenshots.caption: Environment and asset study: building, taxi, character and ground tile with original textures.
Recovered character animation poses: collector, goombah, dog trainer and Russian boss.
Animation study: four poses from a recovered civilian run cycle.

items.title: An empire built on the streets
items.text: Recruit and command a crew, fight rival gangs, take control of businesses and turn income into a stronger organization. The remaster aims to keep the original mix of tactical street encounters and longer-term empire building.

items.title: A familiar world, rebuilt for modern screens
items.text: The new direction preserves the original game’s setting and identity. Work is focused on making its characters, streets and missions easier to read and control while retaining the isometric perspective and atmosphere.

items.title: Recovering the foundations
items.text: The asset inspection has recovered models, textures, animations, maps and supporting game resources. Characters, vehicles and buildings can now be previewed outside the original game, giving the remaster a foundation for visual and animation testing.

items.title: From experiments to a remaster
items.text: Early neighborhood experiments explored crew movement, business capture, income and combat. The project has since shifted toward a shared Godot remaster project for Windows and iOS. The next milestone is a small mission that tests the new interface, imported assets and both control schemes.

items.title: A redesigned interface
items.text: Build a clearer HUD, readable menus and responsive layouts for desktop monitors and smaller touchscreens. PC controls are planned around mouse and keyboard; iPhone and iPad controls around touch selection, command buttons and camera pan and zoom.

items.title: Refreshed sights and sound
items.text: Improve texture resolution, refine models and animation presentation, and update audio quality while keeping the original visual character and mood. The images above document the source asset stage, before those upgrades.

items.title: Quality of life
items.text: Make selecting units, giving orders and understanding mission goals more convenient. Focus on readable information, useful feedback and controls suited to each platform as the first playable mission takes shape.

items.title: Expanded maps and story
items.text: Build toward larger maps, additional story content and more varied objectives after the core remaster experience is working. These are development goals rather than features available in a public build.

items.title: PC and iOS
items.text: Target Windows PC and iPhone/iPad from the same project, with platform-specific controls and graphics settings. iOS support is planned and still needs device testing. Release timing will follow the playable milestones.

items.title: A living criminal city
items.text: Explore pedestrians with daily routines, traffic, working businesses, police patrols and distinct neighborhoods. The city could react to extortion, violence, business ownership and shifting criminal influence even when the player is elsewhere.

items.title: Smarter gangster AI and tactical combat
items.text: Consider cover use, coordinated attacks, retreats, bodyguard behavior and injuries, while preserving Gangland's original real-time crew-command feel and isometric camera.

items.title: A deeper criminal economy
items.text: Explore interconnected protection rackets, gambling, smuggling, loan sharking, legitimate businesses, money laundering and territorial income. Choices could create opportunities, risks and rival responses.

items.title: Gangsters with personalities and consequences
items.text: Investigate loyalty, ambition, greed, fear, relationships, promotions, injuries and betrayal, so crew members develop stories and react to how the family is managed.

items.title: Rival families, diplomacy and territory
items.text: Consider negotiations, temporary alliances, retaliation, contested neighborhoods, rival expansion and police investigations driven by the player's actions.

items.title: Modern graphics, classic Gangland identity
items.text: Keep the recognizable 2004 isometric perspective, colorful urban atmosphere, building proportions and character silhouettes while exploring improved textures, lighting, animations, effects and environmental detail.

items.title: Design principle and development status
items.text: These are ideas under consideration, not features in development or confirmed for release. The priority remains a faithful, playable Gangland remaster. No work on these proposed systems is planned until development resumes at the PC.

games.summary: My next project: an early Gangland remaster aiming for a refreshed interface, improved presentation, expanded content, and PC and iOS support.
